subject.title: [Feature]: Browser sandbox should support non-Docker backends (external CDP/noVNC endpoint)

question: Should sandbox browser support be extended through narrow external CDP/noVNC config fields, or through a more general backend capability contract with explicit CDP/noVNC security requirements?
rationale: This changes a browser-control and sandbox boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the public config shape, lifecycle owner, or security model from source inspection alone.

options.title: Design backend-aware endpoint contract
options.body: Add a versioned sandbox-browser backend or external-endpoint contract with explicit auth, SSRF, noVNC, lifecycle, docs, and tests before exposing the feature.

options.title: Ship narrow external endpoint fields
options.body: Add only opt-in external CDP/noVNC fields if maintainers accept a smaller public config surface and define equivalent validation and security checks.

options.title: Defer to broader browser backend design
options.body: Keep this issue open while the broader browser backend/plugin interface work settles the driver and endpoint abstractions.

recommendation.title: Design backend-aware endpoint contract
recommendation.body: Add a versioned sandbox-browser backend or external-endpoint contract with explicit auth, SSRF, noVNC, lifecycle, docs, and tests before exposing the feature.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across sandbox browser, backend seams, and security defaults touched by this decision.
